data.one_liner: A comprehensive framework for state management, dependency injection, routing, and localization.
data.what_it_does: Flutter Control is a modular framework that streamlines app architecture by combining state management, a built-in service locator, navigation, reactive observables, and localization support.
use_when: You want an all-in-one framework for state management, DI, and routing without wiring multiple small packages.
You prefer modular architecture with independent modules and service locators.
You need reactive state bindings combined with custom lifecycle-aware widgets and hooks.
avoid_when: You prefer single-purpose libraries and want to choose your own state management or routing solution.
You want to avoid heavy framework lock-in.
You rely heavily on compile-time code generation for navigation or state models.
strengths: Comprehensive ecosystem covering state, DI, navigation, and localization in one package.
Built-in Service Locator with Factory and Singleton patterns.
Reactive observables like ActionControl and FieldControl integrated with UI builders.
Context extensions and hooks for lazy initialization and clean lifecycle management.
weaknesses: High level of framework lock-in due to its monolithic approach.
Extensive learning curve to understand all custom architectural concepts and base classes.
data.setup_notes: Initialize the core framework in main.dart using Control.initControl and wrap your app with ControlRoot.

alternatives.name: go_router
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a standard, declarative routing package maintained directly by the Flutter team instead of a framework-specific navigation system.

alternatives.name: auto_route
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer code-generation-based type-safe routing and deep linking.
